subject: Replatform risk: BlueLane capacity ask + competitive test results
thread_summary: BlueLane signaled intent to evaluate a competitor for a replatform; sent benchmark results showing latency delta on long-context inference. Internal save plan proposed: short-term capacity uplift + three-month committed ramp, pilot SLA credits, and targeted discount tied to capacity commit.
messages:
From: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@bluelane.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-30 09:12 PST
Subject: Replatform evaluation & capacity request

Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a quick head-to-head with OrionAI on our dev set and are seeing a consistent 18-22% lower token latency for long-context generation (20k tokens) with their self-hosted pipeline. That gap combined with their aggressive licensing has leadership asking us to open a formal bake-off.

We also have a Q4 demand spike: forecasting +45% peak throughput in Jan. Before we kick off an RFP, wanted to check if Redwood can commit to a short-term capacity uplift and provide the benchmark artifacts you used so our infra team can reproduce.

Priority items for us:
- a runbook for replicating the long-context latency test
- a proposal for a 3-month committed uplift (baseline +45%) and provisional pricing
- a note on fallback behavior if we exceed committed burst during spikes

Can you loop in infra/responses? We'd like an answer and a short proposal by Dec 3.

—Claire
VP Product, BlueLane Analytics

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@bluelane.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-30 13:08 PST
Subject: Re: Replatform evaluation & capacity request

Claire — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the preliminary numbers. We appreciate you surfacing OrionAI early. We're confident Redwood can close the latency delta for the long-context case with two levers: targeted quantization profile + transient dedicated shard for KV-heavy workloads.

Immediate next steps:
1) I'll send an internal sync and benchmark artifacts you can run locally (attached).
2) We can propose a 3-month uplift package: committed capacity + burst buffer and a staged discount tied to the 3-month commit.
3) Monica, can you scope a short SLA credits/uptime fallback for overflow?

We can have a formal proposal by EOD Dec 3. Heads-up: if BlueLane needs private deployment/on-prem for latency parity we can outline that option in the proposal too, but it will change lead time.

Marissa
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Attachments: bluelane-benchmark-report.pdf (benchmark artifacts), mutual-action-plan-v2.xlsx (template)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-01 08:45 PST
Subject: Internal: BlueLane bake-off — quick triage and ask list

Team — Claire sent us the Orion comparison and a hard ask for a 3-day reproducible test plus a 3-month committed uplift. We need a tight save plan with technical talking points and an offer they can share with procurement. Key items:

1) Technical repro: Rishi, can you assemble a one-page runbook + the inference config we used (context window 20k, KV cache warm up pattern, batching config)? They specifically flagged long-context latency.

2) Capacity & pricing: Ben, draft a 3-month uplift proposal: baseline = their current committed Q, uplift = +45% peak, include burst buffer at 1.5x for 2 hours/day, and a staged discount schedule tied to the spend band. Include economy of token cost with our caching.

3) Pilot SLA: Monica, propose a credits schedule if latency SLOs miss by >20% on 3 consecutive days. Also clarify private deployment trade-offs (lead time, infra ops).

4) Negotiation posture: this feels like a competitive displacement ask. If leadership wants to be aggressive I'll need a one-time concession authority (~10%) to convert. Hold that as escalation.

Deadline: package to me by Dec 2 COB so we can deliver Dec 3. I attached the artifacts Claire requested.

—Marissa

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-01 11:03 PST
Subject: Re: Internal: BlueLane bake-off — quick triage and ask list

Marissa — put together a reproducible repro and a plain-language summary for procurement. Highlights:

- Root cause of latency gap: their test used an unsharded KV approach; Redwood's runtime benefits from KV sharding + batched KV retrieval for long contexts. For 20k tokens we see a 12–15% token-latency improvement with our current quantization profile; with the recommended transient dedicated shard we can bridge to ~5% delta.
- Suggested repro steps: warm KV cache with the first 1k tokens, run 10 sustained 5-minute streams at p95 concurrency (we'll include the exact curl commands and config).
- Expected cost/throughput: attaching a quick cost tiers CSV with per-token delta across modes (hosted, dedicated, private).

I'll attach the runbook and the redwood-cost-tiers.csv to the package.

—Rishi, Applied ML / Solutions

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@bluelane.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-03 09:22 PST
Subject: Proposal: 3-month uplift + pilot SLA — BlueLane (BL-2027-0042)

Claire — attaching the uplift proposal and MAP. Short summary:

Offer (3 months):
- Committed uplift: +45% peak capacity (starts Jan 1)
- Burst buffer: 1.5x capacity available for 2 hours per peak day
- Discount: tiered — 7% at baseline uplift, 10% if spend > 1.2x uplift band, 12% for upfront prepay of 2 months
- SLA fallback: up to 10% service credits if p95 latency miss >20% for 3 consecutive days (detailed schedule in MAP)
- Optional: transient dedicated shard configuration for long-context workloads (estimated ops lead time: 5 business days)

Attachments: bluelane-benchmark-report.pdf, bluelane-mutual-action-plan-v2.xlsx, redwood-cost-tiers.csv

We'd like a quick sync to walk through results tomorrow — available windows: Dec 4 10–11am PST or Dec 4 2–3pm PST.

—Ben

From: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@bluelane.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@bluelane.ai>, procurement@bluelane.ai
Date: 2027-12-04 18:05 PST
Subject: Re: Proposal: 3-month uplift + pilot SLA — BlueLane (BL-2027-0042)

Ben / Marissa — thanks for the detailed packet. A few quick notes from leadership and infra after reviewing your runbook and cost tiers:

- The reproducible test reproduced your 12–15% improvement, nice. The transient dedicated shard projection to ~5% delta is material — procurement wants that option priced as an explicit line item.
- The pricing bands look reasonable, but their CFO asked for a softer concession: if we commit to a 3-month uplift, can Redwood match OrionAI's 'first-month at 50% list' introductory concession? That is a major ask.
- Also need clarity on how burst is throttled across regions — some of our traffic originates in EU and will be routed to EU nodes.

We're scheduling a short exec sync to review final tradeoffs on Dec 5 14:00 PST. Can you confirm you can join?

—Claire

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@bluelane.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-05 16:05 PST
Subject: Re: Proposal: 3-month uplift + pilot SLA — BlueLane (BL-2027-0042)

Claire — confirmed, I can join the Dec 5 14:00 PST exec sync. Quick note on the concession ask: I don't have authority for a first-month 50% list concession. Recommended escalation: we offer a targeted one-time onboarding credit equal to ~35% of month-one uplift (applied as prepaid credit toward usage) plus a 10% discount band if they prepay two months. This preserves unit economics while giving visible short-term relief.

On region routing: burst buffer applies per-region by default; we'll honor EU-region burst up to the same 1.5x band on EU nodes but will pro-rate if cross-region failover occurs. Monica will share the exact routing language in the MAP during the call.

Agenda for the exec sync:
- Run quick highlights from the benchmark (Rishi)
- Pricing summary and concession (Ben + Marissa)
- SLA and routing language (Monica)
- Procurement ask and next steps (Claire / Samir)

See you at 14:00 PST. If leadership wants escalation on the concession, please flag during the sync and I will route to Revenue Ops for approval.

—Marissa
[Thread attachments referenced above: bluelane-benchmark-report.pdf (pdf, 2.4MB stub), bluelane-mutual-action-plan-v2.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB stub), redwood-cost-tiers.csv (csv, 8KB stub)]
